Date: 2026-11-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood Solutions), Anika Shah (Head of Search, Olympus Data), Liam O'Connor (Staff ML Engineer), Rita Gomez (Eng Manager), Samir Patel (Product)
summary: Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints walkthrough. Focus on: semantic alignment for product search, latency vs cost tradeoffs, integration via Redwood API and Console, and an outline for a 2-week pilot. Customer asked detailed questions on data residency, KMS integration, and how reranking integrates with their current vector DB. Agreed next steps: security packet, trial keys, pilot scope and pricing.
topics: Console walkthrough: routing and model pinning
Optimize suggestions: batching, KV caching, quantization guidance
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood — with me is Carlos, our search SE, and Priya on solutions.
[00:10] Anika Shah: Hi all, Anika here. We're excited to see how you handle rerank — we've got a pretty large catalog and some tricky relevance issues.
[00:18] Carlos Rivera: Great, thanks Anika. Quick agenda: we'll demo the hosted embeddings endpoint, show the vector + rerank flow, then hop into the Console and Optimize recommendations. We'll leave time for Qs.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Couple constraints from our side: 95th percentile latency under 200ms for the on-site search widget; data must stay in EU region; and encryption keys managed by our KMS.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally noted. We support region pinning for hosted and private capacity options if needed, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private. For hosted, we have regional residency in eu-west and audit logs.
[00:52] Rita Gomez: Also curious about how caching impacts freshness — our catalog updates hourly.
[01:00] Carlos Rivera: Good question. Our prefix/KV cache keeps model KV shards to accelerate generation for repeated prefixes; for embeddings and rerank we recommend short TTLs on cached vectors when the corpus updates frequently. You can tune via the Console.
[01:18] Priya Patel: I'll show a quick run: we have a small sample dataset loaded in the demo project. First call is embeddings.create on the hosted API, returns a 1536-d vector (note: in this demo we simulated with open vector dim). We then compute dot similarity and call the rerank endpoint with top-100 candidates.
[01:40] [screen share noises]
[01:45] Carlos Rivera: So here's the code snippet — POST to /v1/embeddings with model param, payload, and the API key. A couple of tips: batch up to 128 items to reduce per-vector cost, but watch memory. The Console suggests batching thresholds depending on your traffic.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: When you say batching, what's the latency penalty on a single query path? We don't want fuzzy spikes.
[02:14] Carlos Rivera: For single-shot user queries, we prioritize latency SLOs. Continuous batching tries to batch only within tight windows — typical added latency is 5-20ms depending on your config. If you set strict SLOs the runtime will favor immediate dispatch (smaller batch).
[02:32] Anika Shah: Walk me through the rerank call — are we sending raw docs? do you compute embeddings server-side?
[02:38] Carlos Rivera: Two options: you can send the doc candidate IDs and let you compute embeddings client-side and pass vectors, or use our hybrid flow where the server hits your doc store and computes or fetchs vectors on the fly. In hosted mode generally customers precompute document embeddings and store them in their vector DB — we integrate by taking top-K and doing a re-score via our rerank endpoint which accepts query vector + candidate metadata.
[03:00] Rita Gomez: We currently use an in-house vector index with HNSW. Can Redwood rerank results that come from our own index?
[03:06] Carlos Rivera: Yes. The rerank endpoint consumes feature vectors and metadata, so you can pass candidate vectors from HNSW. We do the heavy lift of contextual rerank using the full model and optional structured prompts.
[03:18] Samir Patel: Is the rerank model stateful? like does it use per-session KV?
[03:22] Carlos Rivera: Rerank is stateless per call, but if you're doing a chat product we support KV cache for generative contexts; rerank itself is a scoring model run on the inputs you pass.
[03:34] [transcription glitch] Speaker 3: and the uh — the redwood infe-rents thing —
[03:37] Maya Chen: (laughs) Redwood inference, yep.
[03:40] Anika Shah: Could you show the Console? I want to see the routing policies and model pinning.
[03:44] Priya Patel: Sure — switching to Console — here is the project view, model catalog, and a pinned model version for rerank (we pinned r-3-small for cost, and r-2-high for canary). Console also shows per-route token cost and latency percentiles so you can spot regressions.
[04:05] Liam O'Connor: Do you have built-in evals? we run lots of bench sets to measure MRR and nDCG.
[04:12] Carlos Rivera: Yes, Optimize ties evals to prompt sets. You can create a dataset of queries + relevance labels and run periodic evals; the platform will produce MRR/nDCG curves and alert on regressions.
[04:24] Anika Shah: Security — for hosted, can keys be customer-managed?
[04:28] Carlos Rivera: For hosted we offer encrypted-at-rest with provider KMS; for BYOK you would use Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) to bring your keys to an HSM. We do provide audit logs and SSO SAML for org controls, plus role-based access in the Console.
[04:44] Rita Gomez: Any SOC 2?
[04:46] Maya Chen: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs — we'll send the pack after.
[04:50] [05:00] Priya Patel: Back to the flow — here's a small sample of rerank request: POST /v1/rerank body contains query vector, candidate vectors and metadata. We showed a side-by-side before/after: baseline lexical ranking vs embedding-first retrieval + model rerank. You can see MRR jump in the sample.
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: How much does reranking cost per call relative to embeddings? give me a ballpark.
[05:26] Carlos Rivera: Rerank is a full forward pass so it's heavier than a single embedding; in hosted it's typically 2-4x the per-query cost depending on model size and number of candidates. But if you reduce candidates (top-50 vs top-500) you can cut cost significantly. Optimize helps recommend the knee in that tradeoff.
[05:44] Anika Shah: Could we do a tiered approach — run cheap embed filter then only rerank a small subset?
[05:49] Carlos Rivera: That's exactly the pattern we recommend — cheap ANN to produce top-K, then rerank top-50 with the model.
[05:56] Samir Patel: For our use case, we need A/B test with current ranking. How do rollouts work?
[06:02] Maya Chen: Console supports canary rollouts and route-level policies. You can split traffic, run evals on each variant, and automatically fallback if latency or quality falls below thresholds.
[06:14] [06:20] Anika Shah: About regional routing — if we pin eu-west, will customer data ever leave region for inference?
[06:25] Carlos Rivera: If you pin to eu-west, processing stays in region for hosted. For logs and billing metadata we keep minimal telemetry. For full guarantee you'd choose Dedicated/Private.
[06:36] Rita Gomez: Do you support per-token cost breakdown? we need visibility to product managers.
[06:40] Priya Patel: Yes, Console billing shows per-route and per-model token and vector cost. We also export CSVs to your data warehouse for deeper chargeback.
[06:51] Liam O'Connor: Let's talk latency numbers — can you show a benchmark?
[06:55] Carlos Rivera: I pulled a small internal benchmark: embeddings (single query) median ~35ms in eu-west with our small embedding model; rerank median ~120ms for 50 candidates on a 16GB GPU profile. These are approximate; we'll run your dataset to provide exact numbers.
[07:14] [07:20] Anika Shah: If we do a 1-week benchmark with our dataset, what do you need from us?
[07:25] Maya Chen: We'll need a sample of queries, your candidate retrieval output (top-K) or vector store access, desired SLOs, and a test key. We'll set up a dedicated trial project and run the same testing harness.
[07:37] Liam O'Connor: Any limitations around PII? Our catalog has user-generated content.
[07:42] Carlos Rivera: Hosted needs care with PII; we offer data retention controls, but for strict PII/non-ES data we often recommend Private. We'll include data-flow diagrams in the security pack.
[07:54] [08:00] Anika Shah: One more question — do you support fine-tuning rerank models on our labels?
[08:05] Carlos Rivera: We support two mechanisms: 1) on-platform fine-tuning for supported models (you supply labels), and 2) offline supervised tuning then serve that artifact via Dedicated/Private. For hosted we offer managed tuning for some model families.
[08:20] Rita Gomez: Ok, timeline — if we want a pilot in January, what's realistic?
[08:24] Maya Chen: We can start a pilot in early December for a 2-week proof with trial keys, then production pilot in January.
[08:31] Samir Patel: Pricing ballpark?
[08:34] Maya Chen: We'll send tiered pricing in the follow-up — it'll include hosted API usage rates for embeddings and rerank, plus optional Dedicated baseline if you want reserved capacity.
[08:46] [08:50] Priya Patel: Quick demo wrap: created embeddings, computed similarity, reran scoring — Console showed per-route latency, cost, and suggested Optimize tweaks like smaller batch size for p95 sensitive routes, and quantization recommendation for lower throughput cost.
[09:07] Anika Shah: This was helpful. Next steps?
[09:10] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) We'll share pricing and pilot scope (Maya). 2) Carlos will attach security docs and SOC2 evidence. 3) Priya will provision demo keys and a notebook with the sample dataset. 4) Olympus to share a small query set and top-K retrieval outputs for the benchmark.
[09:27] Liam O'Connor: We'll aim to send sample data by 2026-11-12.
[09:30] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[09:33] [call ends]
